# One cursor scenario per line, for the context rules in src/provider/context.ts.
#
#   <file name> | <language id> | <line, with <> marking the cursor> [| <preceding lines, \n escaped>]
#
# The cursor marker keeps trailing spaces meaningful; the fourth field is the
# document text before the current line (the current line prefix is appended to
# it, exactly as the VS Code layer does).
# Lines starting with # are comments.

notamod.gml | ntgml-legacy | #define <>

# --- the game's own objects, from the generated field table ---------------
# `Player` has an entry in the vendored fields.gml; `MultiMenu` is one of the
# 75 objects the dump does not list, so it is not a known receiver and
# completing after its dot offers nothing.
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | Player.<>
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | Player.we<>
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | MultiMenu.<>
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy |     wep = <> | with (Player) {\n
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy |     my_heal<> | with (Player) {\n
# `on_` after a non-`Custom*` creation resolves to no object at all, not to
# `Player`: only `Custom*` objects have `on_` names, so naming `Player` here
# can only take fields away. The union of every `Custom*` callback is left.
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | var o = instance_create(x, y, Player); o.on_<>
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy |     maxh<> | with (MultiMenu) {\n

# --- how far a `with` receiver reaches ------------------------------------
# The object is in scope for its body and no longer: to the matching `}`, or,
# for the brace-less form, to the end of that one statement. The window is
# masked first, so a `with` written in a comment or a string is not a receiver.
# 1. the block has closed again
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | ammo<> | with (Player) {\n    wep = 1;\n}\n
# 2. brace-less, cursor still on the statement's own line
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | with (Player) my_heal<>
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | with Player my_heal<>
# 3. brace-less, and the statement is over (a `;`, then a new line)
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | ammo<> | with (Player) my_health = 5;\n
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy |     ammo<> | with Player\n
# 4. nested: the inner object wins while both are open, the outer one is back
#    in scope once the inner block closes
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy |         maxh<> | with (Player) {\n    with (CustomEnemy) {\n
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy |     wep<> | with (Player) {\n    with (CustomEnemy) {\n    }\n
# 5. only mentioned in a comment or a string
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | ammo<> | // with (Player) {\n
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | ammo<> | trace("with (Player) {");\n
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | ammo<> | /* with (Player) {\n*/\n

# --- an `on_` word looks only for `Custom*` receivers, and looks far ------
# The callback is normally assigned outside any `with` body, so this path is
# deliberately unbounded - but for that to be safe it must ignore the game's
# own objects, which have no `on_` names to offer.
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | e.on_<> | var e = instance_create(x, y, CustomEnemy);\nwith (Player) { speed = 1; }\n
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy |     on_ste<> | with (CustomEnemy) {\n    with (Player) { speed = 1; }\n
thing.mod.gml | ntgml-legacy | on_<> | with (Player) {\n    speed = 1;\n}\n
